  • Fine-tune open-weight LLMs using SFT, LoRA/QLoRA and post-training methods such as DPO and GRPO

  • Diagnose model failures and turn them into experiments. Decide whether the answer is better data, post-training, prompting or classifiers

  • Build training data and evals that directly shape what gets trained next

  • Improve model behavior across personalization, consistency, tone, multilingual and group interactions

  • Ship to production and use real user behavior to guide the next iteration

  • Speed up the training loop so experiments are faster, easier to compare, and more reproducible

  • You’ve personally post-trained open-weight LLMs for a user-facing product and shipped them to production

  • You’ve worked where AI was core to the product or business, not an experimental side feature

  • You build data and evals yourself and make decisions from evidence

  • You can take work beyond notebooks into production

  • You use AI tools daily in your own engineering work

  • You are fully comfortable working with uncensored models and explicit NSFW content, including harmful material when developing and evaluating moderation system

Bonus points

  • Experience with conversational AI, roleplay products, or highly personalized consumer AI

  • Multilingual LLMs

  • Moderation, safety, or adversarial testing

  • Multimodal models

  • Open-source LLM / post-training contributions

Why EverAI?

📈 Exponential Growth: From 60M users in 3 years, to 100M next — and 500M beyond

🌍 Global Impact: Top-tier user growth, real-world adoption, and cultural relevance

🧠 Proven Leadership: A senior team that’s launched, scaled, and exited & IPO’d multiple scale ups — now fully focused on reshaping AI companionship

👥 Elite Remote Team: 100% remote and built to win — world-class talent from Tier 1 tech companies, with a culture of ownership, velocity, and radical creativity

description: Our Mission At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient. We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today! The Role As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you own our customer deployments end to end. Our system runs on-prem at industrial facilities, critical infrastructure, and military sites, integrated with the cameras, networks, and robots already in place. You survey the site, plan the deployment, install and integrate the system, tune it to the site's conditions, and hand it over to operators who will rely on it daily. You are also the technical face of Laelaps on site. You work with security operators to understand how they actually work and where the bottlenecks are, align with their leadership on what success looks like, and translate what you learn into configuration, code, and product priorities. Early deployments you run alongside the founders; over time you own sites and accounts independently. Expect roughly half your time at customer sites in Switzerland and Europe, and the rest in Zurich, turning field lessons into tooling and automation that make each deployment faster than the last. This is an engineering role with a customer in the room, not a support or services role. What You'll Work On Deployments end-to-end: site surveys, network and hardware planning, installation, camera and VMS integration, commissioning, validation, and handover. On-prem infrastructure: install and manage our stack on edge hardware (NVIDIA DGX Spark, Jetson Thor class devices) inside customer networks, often air-gapped or heavily restricted. Integrations: connect existing cameras, sensors, VMS platforms, and robots into one coordinated system, and write the glue code where no integration exists yet. System tuning: calibrate detection and tracking to each site's terrain, lighting, and threat profile until the system performs in the field as it does in the demo. Pilots to production: make POCs succeed technically, because pilots that work become contracts. Customer understanding: sit with operators, interview stakeholders from the control room to the leadership floor, and map the real problems and bottlenecks behind the stated requirements. Customer trust: train operators, respond fast when something breaks, and be the engineer customers ask for by name. The deployment playbook: turn every hard-won lesson into runbooks, tooling, and automation that compound. Product feedback: bring real field signal back to the core engineering team and shape the roadmap with it. Who We're Looking For We are looking for an engineer who runs toward the messy parts, with the EQ to match the IQ. You are as comfortable in a server room or on a windswept perimeter as you are in a terminal, and just as comfortable in a conversation. You can spend a shift with a security operator and earn enough trust that they tell you what actually goes wrong at 3 a.m., then brief a head of security or a site director in their language, not yours. You listen more than you pitch, you read the room, and you switch registers between the guard house and the boardroom without breaking stride. You debug across the whole stack without ceremony: is it the hardware, the network, the driver, the model, or the config? Above all, you take personal ownership of the outcome: the deployment works because you made it work, and the customer trusts us because you earned it. Your Background 3+ years of relevant software, robotics, embedded systems, or systems integration experience. A Master’s degree in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Strong Python and hands-on C++ experience. You can read, debug, and extend production code in both. Experience deploying and operating software on-prem or at the edge (Docker required; GPU inference experience a strong plus). Experience working with sensors and embedded systems, including device interfaces and communications protocols. High EQ and experience working directly with end users or customers: you can uncover needs, work across stakeholders, and communicate technical issues clearly. Composure in customer-facing technical sessions, including when systems fail and plans need to change. Fluent German and/or French, and good English. Our sites and their operators run in German; the team runs in English. Willingness to travel regularly to customer sites across Switzerland and Europe, with multi-day on-site stints. Based in or willing to relocate to Zurich. Citizenship of Switzerland, an EU/EFTA member state, or a NATO member state, and eligibility for security clearance where customer sites require it. A valid category B driving license. Nice to Have Real networking competence: VLANs, firewalls, routing, VPNs, and debugging connectivity in networks you do not control. Hands-on comfort with hardware: you have racked servers, flashed devices, crimped a cable, or built systems that touch the physical world. Checking cable connections at 2 a.m. at a client site is second nature while debugging an issue on a customer side. Experience with cameras, VMS platforms (Milestone, Genetec, or similar), ONVIF/RTSP, or the physical security industry. Computer vision or ML deployment experience, especially optimising inference on edge GPUs. Robotics experience: ROS2 and Rviz2, robot integration, or fleet operations. Experience in defence, government, or other regulated environments. French, Italian, or another European language. Startup experience, ideally somewhere you were handed a hard problem and a deadline instead of a spec. What We Offer Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end. Our proprietary MIMO-over-copper technology powers a high-performance, chiplet-based AI memory fabric that is both scalable and energy-efficient . Job title: Advanced R&D - Physical Design Engineer Location : Lausanne, Switzerland The Physical Design (PD) Engineer translates high-speed communication IP digital designs into physical GDSII layouts for advanced FinFET nodes. You will bridge logic design, owning block-to-chip implementation from netlist to final physical sign-off, ensuring PPA (Power, Performance, and Area) targets are met. Immediate key objective Drive block-level physical implementation—covering synthesis, SDC constraints, floorplanning, placement, CTS, and routing—meeting strict frequency, area, and power targets. Execute timing closure across multiple corners and modes (MCMM) utilizing static timing analysis (STA) and generating targeted ECOs. Drive full physical verification closure sign-off in deep-submicron FinFET technologies. Responsibility Own block synthesis, floorplanning, placement optimization, CTS, and routing. Develop and refine SDC constraints to ensure design intent matches physical realization. Collaborate with the digital design team to resolve logic or architectural bottlenecks affecting P&R convergence. Generate progress reports, document implementation flows, and prepare sign-off packages for tape-out. Required Experience 5+ years of hands-on physical design experience focusing on synthesis, SDC constraints, CTS, and place and route for high-speed systems. Strong technical background in deep-submicron CMOS/FinFET physical effects, crosstalk, and high-frequency clock network design. Proven experience of taking complex blocks from netlist through successful physical implementation. Direct experience with advanced low-power implementation techniques (UPF, power gating). Proven tape-out experience in advanced FinFET nodes (e.g., 7nm, 5nm, or 3nm). Experience handling complex block-to-chip hierarchical assembly, pin placement, and top-level routing constraints.. Required Skills Expert proficiency with industry-standard implementation and sign-off tools (e.g., Cadence Genus/Innovus/Tempus or Synopsys Design Compiler/ICC2/PrimeTime, and Calibre). Deep understanding of SDC creation, and MCMM timing management. Strong scripting skills (Tcl, Python) for flow automation and design data analysis. Analytical mindset to debug congestion routing issues, and complex timing violations. The Physical Design (PD) Engineer translates high-speed communication IP digital designs into physical GDSII layouts for advanced FinFET nodes. You will bridge logic design, owning block-to-chip implementation from netlist to final physical sign-off, ensuring PPA (Power, Performance, and Area) targets are met.

 

Immediate key objective

  • Drive block-level physical implementation—covering synthesis, SDC constraints, floorplanning, placement, CTS, and routing—meeting strict frequency, area, and power targets.

  • Execute timing closure across multiple corners and modes (MCMM) utilizing static timing analysis (STA) and generating targeted ECOs.

  • Drive full physical verification closure sign-off in deep-submicron FinFET technologies.

Responsibility

  • Own block synthesis, floorplanning, placement optimization, CTS, and routing.

  • Develop and refine SDC constraints to ensure design intent matches physical realization.

  • Collaborate with the digital design team to resolve logic or architectural bottlenecks affecting P&R convergence.

  • Generate progress reports, document implementation flows, and prepare sign-off packages for tape-out.

Required Experience

  • 5+ years of hands-on physical design experience focusing on synthesis, SDC constraints, CTS, and place and route for high-speed systems.

  • Strong technical background in deep-submicron CMOS/FinFET physical effects, crosstalk, and high-frequency clock network design.

  • Proven experience of taking complex blocks from netlist through successful physical implementation.

  • Direct experience with advanced low-power implementation techniques (UPF, power gating).

  • Proven tape-out experience in advanced FinFET nodes (e.g., 7nm, 5nm, or 3nm).

  • Experience handling complex block-to-chip hierarchical assembly, pin placement, and top-level routing constraints..

Required Skills

  • Expert proficiency with industry-standard implementation and sign-off tools (e.g., Cadence Genus/Innovus/Tempus or Synopsys Design Compiler/ICC2/PrimeTime, and Calibre).

  • Deep understanding of SDC creation, and MCMM timing management.

  • Strong scripting skills (Tcl, Python) for flow automation and design data analysis.

  • Analytical mindset to debug congestion routing issues, and complex timing violations.

  • Self-motivated with strong sense of ownership; effective communicator and team player

Required Education

  • Masters or Ph.D. in E.E., Communications or other relevant fields

Shield AI is seeking a high-performing Business Development / Account Executive to drive growth for Hivemind Autonomy across the Netherlands, with a primary focus on defense and government customers. 

This role is responsible for identifying, shaping, and closing complex opportunities while building enduring customer relationships and executing disciplined capture strategies. You will partner closely with Sales Leadership, Product, Engineering, and Strategic Engagement teams to align customer needs with Hivemind’s autonomy capabilities and deliver mission-critical outcomes. 

The ideal candidate is a customer-first, technically credible seller with strong capture instincts, experience navigating defence acquisition processes, and a proven track record of winning and expanding strategic accounts.

  • Identify, qualify, and shape new business opportunities through deep understanding of customer missions, budgets, and acquisition pathways 

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with key decision-makers, program offices, and influencers across defense and government customers 

  • Lead proposal development in partnership with BD Operations and cross-functional teams, ensuring alignment with customer requirements and value propositions 

  • Conduct competitive analysis and position Hivemind effectively in complex, multi-stakeholder environments 

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, and Solutions teams to translate customer needs into compelling technical and operational solutions 

  • Manage deal progression with rigour (qualification, deal strategy, forecasting accuracy, CRM hygiene)

raw.title: Technical Product Manager - AI Finance App
raw.description:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

 

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

 

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit is building a AI Finance Superapp for Southeast Asia across payments, remittance, insurance, wealth, and trading.

 

These products move real money. Reliability, regulatory requirements, and third-party financial rails are fundamental to the product - not considerations around the edges.

 

The Technical Product Manager owns a product vertical end-to-end, from strategy and outcomes through technical design, delivery, and launch.

 

We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where AI genuinely improves an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted.

 

What You'll Own

  • Owning a product vertical end-to-end, including strategy, metrics, roadmap, priorities and delivery.

  • Shaping technical design with engineering across APIs, data flows, ledgering, reconciliation, failure handling, security and scalability.

  • Driving trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability, regulatory requirements and user experience.

  • Building regulatory requirements into the product across KYC, transaction monitoring, limits, privacy and licensing.

  • Applying AI where it improves outcomes, with clear evaluation, safeguards, human oversight and failure handling.

  • Shipping products around external dependencies, including regulatory approvals, financial rails and third-party partners.

  • Aligning Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance around clear product decisions and launch requirements.

     

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of complex technical products from strategy through production.

  • Strong technical foundation across system architecture, APIs, databases, workflows, failure modes and distributed systems.

  • Experience working closely with engineers and ability to review, challenge and contribute to technical designs.

  • Experience in payments, banking, remittance, insurance, trading or another regulated, high-consequence product domain.

  • Strong product judgment and ability to make difficult trade-offs under technical, regulatory and operational constraints.

  • Experience building with LLMs or AI products, including evaluation, reliability and understanding when AI should not be used.

     

Nice to have

  • Engineering or highly technical product background.

  • Experience building zero-to-one fintech or consumer products.

  • Experience defining evaluation frameworks for ML or LLM-powered products.

     

Outcome

  • Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap

  • Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch

  • Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds

  • AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted

  • Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged

  • Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

 

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

 

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit builds technology products used by millions of users across Southeast Asia. As our products and systems scale, we need technical leaders who can solve difficult engineering problems and raise the engineering bar around them.

The Staff Software Engineer owns technical direction and execution for major products and systems. This is a hands-on role - you will design systems, write code, and drive critical engineering work from idea to production.

 

What You'll Own

  • Owning technical design and execution for major products, systems and engineering initiatives.

  • Designing scalable, reliable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Building alongside the team through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Driving architecture decisions and trade-offs across speed, scalability, reliability, cost and maintainability.

  • Turning ambiguous product problems into clear technical solutions and execution plans.

  • Raising engineering quality through stronger system design, testing, security, observability and development practices.

  • Leading technically critical initiatives and mentoring engineers across teams.

 

What We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep expertise in backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Track record of technically leading major engineering projects from design through production.

  • Ability to make sound technical trade-offs, influence engineers and solve complex production problems.

 

Nice to have

  • Experience scaling engineering teams, systems or development practices through significant growth.

  • Experience operating across multiple products, markets or countries.

 

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

 

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

 

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

raw.description:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, accessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who love building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who care about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it’s the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As Head of Compliance and AML at Doit Lithuania, you will build and run our compliance and anti-money-laundering function from day one.

You will act as our Compliance Officer and AML Officer, and report directly to the management board. You will be independent of the business lines you monitor. You will run compliance and AML for a digital investment platform serving clients in Lithuania and across the European Economic Area.

What You’ll Own

  • Write and own the compliance and AML/CTF policies and procedures.

  • Build the business-wide AML risk assessment, customer risk scoring and risk appetite.

  • Design remote onboarding controls with our KYC partners, including enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk clients.

  • Design and tune transaction monitoring scenarios for brokerage activity.

  • Run sanctions screening at onboarding, on an ongoing basis and on payments.

  • File suspicious activity reports with the FNTT and suspicious order reports under MAR.

  • Run the compliance monitoring programme and report to the board.

  • Approve marketing communications and oversee product governance, complaints and conflicts of interest.

  • Manage the regulatory relationship with the Bank of Lithuania on compliance and AML matters.

  • Prepare the firm for the EU AML Regulation, which applies from July 2027.

  • Build the compliance and AML team as the business grows.

What We’re Looking For

  • Significant experience in AML/CTF at a regulated EU financial institution. Ideally at an investment firm, neobroker, neobank or e-money institution.

  • Experience with digital onboarding and remote identity verification at scale.

  • Hands-on experience building risk assessments, monitoring scenarios and EDD processes.

  • Experience filing suspicious activity reports and handling regulatory inspections.

  • Knowledge of MiFID II conduct and investment-services compliance, or the ability to learn it fast.

  • Experience selecting and overseeing KYC, screening and monitoring tools.

  • Strong judgment and the confidence to challenge senior colleagues.

  • Clear, concise writing for policies, board reports and regulators.

  • A clean record and good reputation, suitable for regulatory approval as a key function holder.

  • Based in Lithuania, or open to relocating to Lithuania.

Nice to Have

  • Lithuanian language ability.

  • An existing working relationship with the Bank of Lithuania or the FNTT.

  • Knowledge of Lithuanian AML law and Bank of Lithuania instructions.

  • Experience with clients across several EEA countries.

  • CAMS (ACAMS) or ICA certification.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only want to attend meetings.

  • Candidates who cannot follow up aggressively and professionally.

  • People who copy policies from templates without fitting them to the business.

  • People who say no without offering a compliant way forward.

  • People who produce long updates without clear decisions or next actions.

Location

This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.

You must be a European citizen or already hold a valid right to work in Lithuania. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Role-specific interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process.

Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritised.

description: Who We Are You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today. We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover. Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI. Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate. Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale. About the team Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people. About the role Evaluation is the core of everything we do. We build from the evals: we define how success will be measured before developing a capability, and use the results to guide training, model selection and deployment. We already have hundreds of evaluations spanning domain knowledge, commerce and gaming, with plans to expand their coverage, depth and scale. This work builds on ProLLM, the public benchmarking platform we ran for real-world use cases until our coding assistant benchmarks became saturated. Since then it has been a private benchmarking platform for Prosus companies. We plan to open it again to publish our commerce benchmarks, covering both agentic and decision-making tasks. We’re looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to own the development of these evaluations and the platform that runs them. The work involves defining meaningful tasks, curating evaluation data, implementing reliable scoring, investigating model behaviour and making results useful for research and product decisions. In our flat team of around 30 engineers, you’ll work directly with applied scientists, training engineers and domain experts. You’ll help teams contribute evaluations and build the infrastructure and automation needed to run them throughout model development. In the first three months, we expect you to take technical ownership of part of the evaluation platform, deliver a set of new or improved evaluations with curated data and calibrated difficulty, and work with scientists to use them in a training or release decision. What the role involves Design evaluations with scientists and domain experts, translating intended capabilities into representative tasks, datasets and success criteria. Cover current applications and capabilities we want future models to acquire. Curate evaluation data and calibrate task difficulty, so that evaluations are neither saturated nor out of reach and still separate models of different quality. Work with domain experts on sourcing, annotation and review, within data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy requirements. Own the development and operation of the evaluation platform across training checkpoints, deployed models and external baselines. Support distributed execution, reproducible configurations, trace inspection and comparison of results, while managing runtime and cost. Develop programmatic checks, outcome-based scoring and LLM-based graders. Calibrate automated judgments against expert reviews, investigate disagreements and test whether graders reward superficial answers or reject valid solutions. Analyse model outputs and agent trajectories, including tool calls, environment state and task outcomes. Distinguish model failures from problems in the evaluation, quantify uncertainty and explain what changed between versions. Maintain versioned tasks, datasets, graders and environments, with protected held-out tests and contamination checks. Expand coverage as models improve, retaining useful regression tests and adding harder tasks where existing tests no longer distinguish performance. Prepare commerce benchmarks for public release on ProLLM, including public mirror sets and evaluation code, where the data can be shared. Integrate evaluations into training and release workflows, with dashboards and regression checks that support concrete decisions. Work with portfolio teams to establish whether offline improvements correspond to better outcomes in online experiments. Build tools and agents that help generate candidate tasks, run evaluations and investigate failures, validating their outputs before adoption. Review contributions and mentor engineers so teams can extend the suite consistently. Minimum qualifications At least five years of ML or software engineering experience, including substantial hands-on work building and evaluating ML systems. Experience owning evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or model-quality systems that informed training or deployment decisions. Strong Python and experience with PyTorch, Transformers or comparable ML libraries, alongside reliable production software development. Practical knowledge of experimental design and statistics, including sampling, uncertainty, repeated trials and comparisons across model versions. Experience running inference or evaluation workloads at scale and debugging failures across models, data, scoring code and infrastructure. Clear communication and the ability to turn ambiguous results into defensible recommendations. Preferred qualifications Experience with language-model training or post-training. Experience with agent or gaming environments. Experience with human evaluation, LLM-as-judge calibration, recommendation metrics or online experimentation. Contributions to evaluation frameworks, public benchmarks or research. What we offer Ownership of the evaluation platform and the evaluations that guide LCM’s research, training and deployment. Access to proprietary domain data, GPU infrastructure and external models for comparison. Direct collaboration with researchers, engineers and portfolio teams, with scope to publish methods and benchmarks, including through ProLLM, where the work can be shared. Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems. Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants. A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role. Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people. About the role We’re looking for experienced applied scientists in two tracks: pre-training, and post-training and continual learning. Each scientist will own a focused research direction within a track. The areas below describe the team’s research agenda; we are looking for depth in one or more of them. The role involves designing experiments, writing the code to run them, analysing results and developing training methods that other teams can use. Scientists own the research questions, training objectives and evidence needed to decide whether a change works, and work with ML engineers to turn successful experiments into reliable training runs. We are a team of around 30 engineers with a flat structure, working directly with portfolio companies to define problems, evaluate models and bring successful work into production. In the first three months, the expectation is to establish strong baselines in a chosen research area, develop and evaluate an improvement, and work with the relevant teams to test it in a downstream application. Track 1: Pre-training This track focuses on continued pre-training of open-weight models on commerce data, including how we represent that data, allocate training compute and transfer capabilities to smaller models. Research areas include: Studying scaling behaviour, data mixtures and compute allocation to decide what goes into the next training run. Developing mid-training methods, including data refinement, annealing schedules, context extension and alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants. Designing training sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, and studying how representations transfer across companies, languages and commerce categories. Building synthetic data pipelines and measuring their contribution through controlled comparisons with real data. Distilling the base model into smaller models, including through on-policy distillation, and measuring the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency. Developing evaluations that help select pre-training runs and predict downstream performance, including checks for temporal leakage, generalisation to new users and items, and retention of existing capabilities. Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation: pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data, using synthetic and real tables and comparing results with established tabular methods. Relevant experience includes continued pre-training or mid-training, data mixture research, scaling laws, tokenisation, entity representations, distillation, or tabular foundation models such as TabPFN and TabICL. Track 2: Post-training and continual learning This track focuses on adapting LCM to commerce tasks and learning from interactions after deployment. The goal is to turn signals from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio into regular updates to model weights, while retaining the capabilities the model has already learned. Research areas include: Developing post-training methods using supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation such as DPO, and reinforcement learning with verifiable or learned rewards, including GRPO and PPO. Learning from session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback. This includes data selection, credit assignment and reward design that account for exposure bias, delayed outcomes and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value. Studying how to combine new interactions with historical data, how frequently to update models, when an update is ready for deployment, and how to preserve performance as user behaviour and catalogues change. Building RL environments with simulated users, catalogues and multi-step commerce tasks, including inspecting trajectories, validating rewards and testing whether improvements in simulation transfer to real interactions. Developing reward models and LLM-based graders, calibrating them against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and testing for reward hacking, sycophancy and excessive concentration on popular items. Training decision models for rankings, offers and promotions using contextual bandits or offline RL, with off-policy evaluation to estimate value and uncertainty, identify gaps in the available evidence and inform controlled online experiments. Developing automated experiments that propose and test changes to training methods, prompts, tools or agent control flow, evaluated on held-out tasks and regression tests before acceptance. Relevant experience includes language-model post-training, reinforcement learning, reward modelling, agent training environments, continual learning, or offline RL and bandits applied to real decisions. The training experience required will depend on the research direction. Responsibilities across both tracks Define success with portfolio teams and evaluate models against strong baselines, including existing production systems, accounting for inference cost, latency and the business outcome the model is meant to improve. Design reproducible experiments with appropriate ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis, using future-period and held-out evaluations, and test whether offline improvements hold online. Work with data and engineering teams on provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories. Publish research and contribute models, benchmarks, environments and training methods to open source where the work and data can be shared. Mentor colleagues, review experiment designs and communicate findings clearly enough to support training and deployment decisions. At least five years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with hands-on experience designing and running model-training experiments. For Track 1, this should include pre-training or mid-training of language models. For Track 2, it should include language-model post-training, or reinforcement learning and decision-model training relevant to the specialisation. Evidence of original research through papers, released models, public benchmarks, open-source projects or significant research contributions to deployed systems. Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with experience implementing experiments and debugging training runs in a shared research codebase. Work on large language models requires hands-on experience with distributed training. Sound experimental judgment, including strong baselines, statistical analysis and the willingness to report negative results. Clear written and verbal communication. Research in recommender systems, generative retrieval, semantic IDs or user behaviour modelling. Experience with synthetic data, model distillation or compression for production. Experience working with marketplace or commerce data and evaluating changes through online experiments. What we offer Autonomy to design experiments and make technical decisions within your research direction. Proprietary commerce data, B300 and H200 GPUs for large-scale training, and external models for evaluation and benchmarking. The opportunity to take research from early experiments through publication and deployment, working directly with portfolio teams on products used by millions of people. Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems. Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role

We’re looking for experienced applied scientists in two tracks: pre-training, and post-training and continual learning. Each scientist will own a focused research direction within a track. The areas below describe the team’s research agenda; we are looking for depth in one or more of them.

The role involves designing experiments, writing the code to run them, analysing results and developing training methods that other teams can use. Scientists own the research questions, training objectives and evidence needed to decide whether a change works, and work with ML engineers to turn successful experiments into reliable training runs. We are a team of around 30 engineers with a flat structure, working directly with portfolio companies to define problems, evaluate models and bring successful work into production.

In the first three months, the expectation is to establish strong baselines in a chosen research area, develop and evaluate an improvement, and work with the relevant teams to test it in a downstream application.

Track 1: Pre-training

This track focuses on continued pre-training of open-weight models on commerce data, including how we represent that data, allocate training compute and transfer capabilities to smaller models. Research areas include:

  • Studying scaling behaviour, data mixtures and compute allocation to decide what goes into the next training run.

  • Developing mid-training methods, including data refinement, annealing schedules, context extension and alignment between text and semantic IDs for users, items and merchants.

  • Designing training sequences from user histories, merchant catalogues and market data, and studying how representations transfer across companies, languages and commerce categories.

  • Building synthetic data pipelines and measuring their contribution through controlled comparisons with real data.

  • Distilling the base model into smaller models, including through on-policy distillation, and measuring the trade-offs between quality, inference cost and latency.

  • Developing evaluations that help select pre-training runs and predict downstream performance, including checks for temporal leakage, generalisation to new users and items, and retention of existing capabilities.

  • Tabular foundation models are a possible specialisation: pre-training and in-context learning on structured commerce data, using synthetic and real tables and comparing results with established tabular methods.

Relevant experience includes continued pre-training or mid-training, data mixture research, scaling laws, tokenisation, entity representations, distillation, or tabular foundation models such as TabPFN and TabICL.

Track 2: Post-training and continual learning

This track focuses on adapting LCM to commerce tasks and learning from interactions after deployment. The goal is to turn signals from a continuous stream of billions of user sessions across the portfolio into regular updates to model weights, while retaining the capabilities the model has already learned. Research areas include:

  • Developing post-training methods using supervised fine-tuning, preference optimisation such as DPO, and reinforcement learning with verifiable or learned rewards, including GRPO and PPO.

  • Learning from session histories, searches, clicks, purchases, repeat orders and operator feedback. This includes data selection, credit assignment and reward design that account for exposure bias, delayed outcomes and the difference between observed engagement and incremental business value.

  • Studying how to combine new interactions with historical data, how frequently to update models, when an update is ready for deployment, and how to preserve performance as user behaviour and catalogues change.

  • Building RL environments with simulated users, catalogues and multi-step commerce tasks, including inspecting trajectories, validating rewards and testing whether improvements in simulation transfer to real interactions.

  • Developing reward models and LLM-based graders, calibrating them against expert judgments and observed outcomes, and testing for reward hacking, sycophancy and excessive concentration on popular items.

  • Training decision models for rankings, offers and promotions using contextual bandits or offline RL, with off-policy evaluation to estimate value and uncertainty, identify gaps in the available evidence and inform controlled online experiments.

  • Developing automated experiments that propose and test changes to training methods, prompts, tools or agent control flow, evaluated on held-out tasks and regression tests before acceptance.

Relevant experience includes language-model post-training, reinforcement learning, reward modelling, agent training environments, continual learning, or offline RL and bandits applied to real decisions. The training experience required will depend on the research direction.

Responsibilities across both tracks

  • Define success with portfolio teams and evaluate models against strong baselines, including existing production systems, accounting for inference cost, latency and the business outcome the model is meant to improve.

  • Design reproducible experiments with appropriate ablations, uncertainty estimates and failure analysis, using future-period and held-out evaluations, and test whether offline improvements hold online.

  • Work with data and engineering teams on provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories.

  • Publish research and contribute models, benchmarks, environments and training methods to open source where the work and data can be shared.

  • Mentor colleagues, review experiment designs and communicate findings clearly enough to support training and deployment decisions.

Minimum qualifications

  • A PhD or equivalent industry research experience in machine learning, computer science, statistics or a related field.

  • At least five years of research or applied science experience in machine learning, including doctoral research, with hands-on experience designing and running model-training experiments. For Track 1, this should include pre-training or mid-training of language models. For Track 2, it should include language-model post-training, or reinforcement learning and decision-model training relevant to the specialisation.

  • Evidence of original research through papers, released models, public benchmarks, open-source projects or significant research contributions to deployed systems.

  • Strong Python and PyTorch skills, with experience implementing experiments and debugging training runs in a shared research codebase. Work on large language models requires hands-on experience with distributed training.

  • Sound experimental judgment, including strong baselines, statistical analysis and the willingness to report negative results.

  • Clear written and verbal communication.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience implementing and debugging training methods in frameworks such as Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, NeMo RL, verl or OpenRLHF, depending on the chosen track.

  • Research in recommender systems, generative retrieval, semantic IDs or user behaviour modelling.

  • Experience with synthetic data, model distillation or compression for production.

  • Experience working with marketplace or commerce data and evaluating changes through online experiments.

What we offer

  • Autonomy to design experiments and make technical decisions within your research direction.

  • Proprietary commerce data, B300 and H200 GPUs for large-scale training, and external models for evaluation and benchmarking.

  • The opportunity to take research from early experiments through publication and deployment, working directly with portfolio teams on products used by millions of people.

  • Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

  • An uncapped budget to recruit and mentor research interns for your projects, with access to candidates through our connections with leading universities.

  • Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

  • A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

  • Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

How to apply

If you want to work on these problems, we would like to hear from you. Please indicate the track and research areas that best match your experience, and include examples of work that show your contribution.

Why Prosus?

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

raw.title: Senior Data Engineer, Training Data Platform
raw.description:
Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, ecommerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role

We’re looking for a senior data engineer to build and operate LCM’s training-data platform, covering acquisition, processing, synthetic generation, quality evaluation and dataset versioning.

Our core data includes events, sessions, orders, catalogues and feedback, supplemented by external sources and generated examples. In our flat team of around 30 engineers, you’ll work with scientists and ML engineers to turn these sources into reproducible datasets and measure how changes to the data affect model performance. You’ll also build tools and agents that automate preparation, task design and quality analysis.

In the first three months, we expect you to take ownership of a part of the platform, such as a pipeline, the dataset versioning layer or the quality checks, deliver a reproducible dataset that a research project uses in a training run, and work with scientists to measure how your data changes affect model quality.

What the role involves

  • Build acquisition and processing pipelines for portfolio data and relevant public and licensed sources, including connectors and content extraction. Turn commerce records into ordered histories and link behaviour to outcomes without leaking future information.

  • Develop the shared platform for inspecting sources, configuring processing and publishing training datasets. Operate distributed workflows, monitor reliability and cost, and implement access controls and retention requirements.

  • Work with scientists, engineers and the relevant teams on data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy-aware handling of customer histories.

  • Implement dataset versioning and lineage across source snapshots, processing code and dataset configurations, so releases can be reproduced and traced to the training runs that used them.

  • Build quality checks for completeness, freshness, duplication, extraction accuracy and coverage. Combine automated checks with sampled review to investigate problems that aggregate metrics can miss.

  • Provide tools for source tagging, sampling and weighting, and maintain evaluation datasets with temporal splits and overlap checks. Work with scientists on controlled comparisons to establish whether data changes improve model quality.

  • Build synthetic data pipelines supporting pre- and post-training, including instruction examples, preference data and agent trajectories. Implement generation, validation, scoring and filtering. Work with the research team to measure how the generated data affects model performance, and manage generation throughput and cost.

  • Build agents that turn catalogue sources into training datasets: propose tasks based on available data and target model capabilities, configure processing and generation, curate outputs and investigate quality failures. Keep agent actions traceable and validate proposed changes before dataset release.

Minimum qualifications

  • At least five years of relevant data engineering experience, including ownership of substantial production pipelines.

  • Strong Python and SQL, with experience writing tested, maintainable code.

  • Hands-on experience with distributed processing using Spark, Ray, Beam or a comparable framework.

  • Experience with cloud storage, workflow orchestration and operating pipelines through source changes, failures and backfills.

  • Practical knowledge of data quality, versioning and lineage, and the ability to translate evolving research requirements into reliable implementations.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with LLM datasets, commerce data, content extraction, synthetic data generation or agents for data tasks.

  • Experience with AWS, Databricks or EMR.

  • Strong distributed-data engineering experience is welcome without prior experience on an LLM team.

What we offer

  • Ownership of the platform supplying LCM’s training and evaluation data, with direct collaboration with researchers and ML engineers.

  • Access to proprietary commerce datasets, distributed processing infrastructure and models for generation and evaluation.

  • Scope to make technical decisions and build reusable tools across portfolio companies.

  • Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

  • Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

  • A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

  • Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

If you’ve built data systems at scale and want to help shape what a foundation model can do, we’d like to hear from you. Tell us about something you’ve built, the challenges involved and the difference it made.

Why Prosus?

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.

Curious about our perks and benefits? Take a look at this page.

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have.
